title: COVID Has a Summer Season Too
hook: Every summer since the pandemic began, COVID cases have climbed — and 2026 is no exception. Unlike flu, COVID doesn't wait for winter.
key_points: COVID cases are ticking up again in summer 2026, as in every prior summer.
This summer pattern has repeated since the pandemic began — it's not a fluke.
COVID differs from flu, which is far more tightly confined to the cold months.
Summer waves get less attention because other health stories crowd them out.
Practical read: don't treat 'not flu season' as 'not respiratory virus season.'
content_html: COVID-19 cases are ramping up again this August. That's not a twist — it's the pattern. Every summer since the pandemic began has brought a rise in cases, and 2026 is following the same script.
extra_html:
It's worth understanding why this catches people off guard. We've been trained by flu to think of respiratory illness as a winter thing: flu is strongly seasonal, tied to cold weather and indoor crowding. COVID has never behaved that way. It produces waves in both summer and winter, driven more by waning immunity and new variants than by the calendar.

The summer versions tend to go unnoticed, partly because other health stories crowd the headlines and partly because nobody expects to catch a respiratory virus in August. The practical adjustment is small: if you're sick in the summer with respiratory symptoms, COVID is a live possibility worth testing for, and being up to date on vaccination isn't a winter-only consideration — especially if you're older or have someone vulnerable at home.

related.title: Cold, Flu, or COVID?
related.hook: They share a lot of symptoms, but colds, flu, and COVID-19 differ in how fast they hit and how hard — and telling them apart can change what you do next.

related.title: Flu and Seasonal Shots
related.hook: Some vaccines are a yearly habit, not a one-time event — because the viruses change, or immunity fades, and a fresh shot keeps protection current each season.

related.title: Caring for a Cold or Flu at Home
related.hook: Most colds and flu run their course on their own. Good home care is about comfort and rest — and knowing the handful of red flags that mean it's time to get checked.

flashcards.prompt: How does COVID's seasonal pattern differ from flu's?

choices.text: COVID also surges in summer; flu is far more confined to cold months
COVID only circulates in winter, unlike flu
Neither has any seasonal pattern at all

flashcards.explanation_html: COVID cases have ticked up every summer since the pandemic began, whereas flu is much more tightly tied to the winter season.

flashcards.prompt: Why do summer COVID waves tend to get little attention?
flashcards.back_html: They're crowded out — other health threats make bigger headlines, and people associate respiratory illness with winter.
